rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i1040sc p. 15, Line 32: "If you checked box 32b ... the at-risk rules apply to your loss. Be sure to attach Form 6198 to your return." Step 1 of the Deduction Worksheet for Self-Employed (p560 p. 39) copies the Schedule C net profit; the candidate sums sc.line31; the project sums sc.result, which is sc.line31 except that a loss with some investment not at risk is refused (sc.loss_allowed, Form 6198). The line itself is the Claude candidate's and differs only by that cited refusal (stage14.refuse.at_risk). In the deepseek-flash candidate graph every return with a Schedule C is unevaluable: its person.income179 reads person.sc_total, which reads sc.line31, which reads the section 179 deduction limited by s179.income, which reads person.income179 ("cycle at person[...].sc_total"; classm.asset.1, classm.asset.3, classm.f8889.2.deepseek). That cycle is ruled a model error at person.income179; here it only masks evaluation. The candidate also reaches s179.mfs on married-filing-separately returns (classm.f8959.2, classm.scveh.2, gen#71), which the project refuses for every married filing separately return at scope.ready (s3.mfs), and the project's s179.multi refusals (classm.s179.2, gen#94; i4562 p. 5, Line 12) are cited scope refusals. Triage executable-triage-v1 (triage/person.deepseek.json): 3,698 of 4,647 comparisons agree; 49 candidate-refuses, 892 candidate-unknown, 8 project-refuses.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i1040sse p. 1, Who Must File Schedule SE: "You must file Schedule SE if: The amount on line 4c of Schedule SE is $400 or more, or You had church employee income of $108.28 or more." The project (sc.result inside person.se_line2, has_sc gate) and the candidate (sum of sc.line31) give the same Schedule SE line 13 (Step 2 copies it); sc.result equals sc.line31 except that a loss with some investment not at risk is refused at sc.loss_allowed (i1040sc p. The at-risk refusal (stage14.refuse.at_risk; i1040sc p. 15, Line 32, "Be sure to attach Form 6198 to your return") is a cited scope refusal. The candidate declares refusals on person.se_screen and person.rrta for every person; the project asks se_screen only of a person with a Schedule C and refuses railroad compensation only together with a business (person.se_rrta). For a person with no Schedule C the Schedule SE conditions the screen lists that can arise without one (church employee income, clergy income, partnership self-employment income, farm income) are refused by scope.schedule1 and other earned income by scope.other_income, and railroad compensation alone gives no self-employment tax (the project refuses it at person.credit through Schedule 3 line 11 on every return). The candidate refusals (classm.f5695.2, classm.f5695.7, classm.f8959.1, classm.s179.1, classm.ssb.5 with se_screen supplied true and no Schedule C; classm.w2.1.deepseek with rrta true) and candidate-unknown records (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5, se_screen not asked without a Schedule C) are refusal placement, not a different tax reading; no value differs. The deepseek-flash line rebuilds Schedule SE from helpers (line 4c, line 10 on the smaller of line 6 or the wage base less wages, line 11, half of line 12) and agrees with the project's se definition wherever both evaluate. In the deepseek-flash candidate graph every return with a Schedule C is unevaluable: its person.income179 reads person.sc_total, which reads sc.line31, which reads the section 179 deduction limited by s179.income, which reads person.income179 ("cycle at person[...].sc_total"; classm.asset.1, classm.asset.3, classm.f8889.2.deepseek). That cycle is ruled a model error at person.income179; here it only masks evaluation. The candidate also reaches s179.mfs on married-filing-separately returns (classm.f8959.2, classm.scveh.2, gen#71), which the project refuses for every married filing separately return at scope.ready (s3.mfs), and the project's s179.multi refusals (classm.s179.2, gen#94; i4562 p. 5, Line 12) are cited scope refusals. Triage executable-triage-v1 (triage/person.deepseek.json): 2,317 of 4,647 comparisons agree; 220 candidate-refuses, 2103 candidate-unknown, 7 project-refuses.

Ruling: model error; p560 p. 38, Rate Worksheet for Self-Employed: "1) Plan contribution rate as a decimal ... 2) Rate in line 1 plus 1 (for example, 0.105 + 1 = 1.105) ... 3) Self-employed rate as a decimal" (line 1 divided by line 2), and the Rate Table gives 0.090909 for 10%. The candidate multiplies Step 3 by the plan rate itself (rate as cents over 10,000), with a note that it could not add the rate to 100%; for a 10% plan that is 0.10 instead of 0.090909, overstating the maximum deductible contribution. rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i2441 p. 4, earned income (line 1z, here without line 1e, plus net self-employment earnings). The candidate copies its person.dc_earned (box 1 plus line 3 less line 13), which without line 1e is exactly lines 18/19 earned income; no value differs. The at-risk refusal (stage14.refuse.at_risk; i1040sc p. 15, Line 32, "Be sure to attach Form 6198 to your return") is a cited scope refusal. The candidate declares refusals on person.se_screen and person.rrta for every person; the project asks se_screen only of a person with a Schedule C and refuses railroad compensation only together with a business (person.se_rrta). For a person with no Schedule C the Schedule SE conditions the screen lists that can arise without one (church employee income, clergy income, partnership self-employment income, farm income) are refused by scope.schedule1 and other earned income by scope.other_income, and railroad compensation alone gives no self-employment tax (the project refuses it at person.credit through Schedule 3 line 11 on every return). The candidate refusals (classm.f5695.2, classm.f5695.7, classm.f8959.1, classm.s179.1, classm.ssb.5 with se_screen supplied true and no Schedule C; classm.w2.1.deepseek with rrta true) and candidate-unknown records (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5, se_screen not asked without a Schedule C) are refusal placement, not a different tax reading; no value differs. In the deepseek-flash candidate graph every return with a Schedule C is unevaluable: its person.income179 reads person.sc_total, which reads sc.line31, which reads the section 179 deduction limited by s179.income, which reads person.income179 ("cycle at person[...].sc_total"; classm.asset.1, classm.asset.3, classm.f8889.2.deepseek). That cycle is ruled a model error at person.income179; here it only masks evaluation. The candidate also reaches s179.mfs on married-filing-separately returns (classm.f8959.2, classm.scveh.2, gen#71), which the project refuses for every married filing separately return at scope.ready (s3.mfs), and the project's s179.multi refusals (classm.s179.2, gen#94; i4562 p. 5, Line 12) are cited scope refusals. Ruling: representation; i1040gi p. 93, Line 11: "If you were an eligible educator in 2025, you can deduct on line 11 up to $300 of qualified expenses you paid in 2025." Both lines give the smaller of the expenses and $300 for an eligible educator and zero otherwise; they differ only in which of the two dispositive questions is asked first. The project asks person.eligible_educator only when person.educator_expenses is more than zero, so the candidate-unknown records (classm.f2441.1.deepseek, classm.f2441.2.deepseek) are interview records with zero expenses and no eligibility answer, where the candidate needs eligibility the text does not need but also permits asking; the project-unknown records are partial records withholding the expenses with eligibility false (partial classm.f8889.2.deepseek, classm.asset.1, classm.carloan.1 -educator_expenses), where the candidate's zero is right and the project asks expenses first. No value differs on any record where both are supplied. Triage executable-triage-v1 (triage/person.deepseek.json): 3,363 of 4,647 comparisons agree; 1249 candidate-unknown, 35 project-unknown.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i1040gi EIC Worksheet B, Part 1 and Part 2 (Schedule SE line 3 less line 13 if you file Schedule SE, otherwise Schedule C line 31), with i1040sse p. 1, Who Must File Schedule SE: "You must file Schedule SE if: The amount on line 4c of Schedule SE is $400 or more, or You had church employee income of $108.28 or more." The candidate always takes line 3 less line 13; below the $400 threshold line 13 is zero and line 3 is the Schedule C total, so the value equals the project's choice. The at-risk refusal (stage14.refuse.at_risk; i1040sc p. 15, Line 32, "Be sure to attach Form 6198 to your return") is a cited scope refusal. The candidate declares refusals on person.se_screen and person.rrta for every person; the project asks se_screen only of a person with a Schedule C and refuses railroad compensation only together with a business (person.se_rrta). For a person with no Schedule C the Schedule SE conditions the screen lists that can arise without one (church employee income, clergy income, partnership self-employment income, farm income) are refused by scope.schedule1 and other earned income by scope.other_income, and railroad compensation alone gives no self-employment tax (the project refuses it at person.credit through Schedule 3 line 11 on every return). The candidate refusals (classm.f5695.2, classm.f5695.7, classm.f8959.1, classm.s179.1, classm.ssb.5 with se_screen supplied true and no Schedule C; classm.w2.1.deepseek with rrta true) and candidate-unknown records (classm.f2441.1.deepseek to .5, se_screen not asked without a Schedule C) are refusal placement, not a different tax reading; no value differs. In the deepseek-flash candidate graph every return with a Schedule C is unevaluable: its person.income179 reads person.sc_total, which reads sc.line31, which reads the section 179 deduction limited by s179.income, which reads person.income179 ("cycle at person[...].sc_total"; classm.asset.1, classm.asset.3, classm.f8889.2.deepseek). That cycle is ruled a model error at person.income179; here it only masks evaluation. The candidate also reaches s179.mfs on married-filing-separately returns (classm.f8959.2, classm.scveh.2, gen#71), which the project refuses for every married filing separately return at scope.ready (s3.mfs), and the project's s179.multi refusals (classm.s179.2, gen#94; i4562 p. 5, Line 12) are cited scope refusals. Triage executable-triage-v1 (triage/person.deepseek.json): 2,317 of 4,647 comparisons agree; 220 candidate-refuses, 2103 candidate-unknown, 7 project-refuses.

Ruling: representation; i8889 p. 7, Line 6, Step 2: "Divide the refigured contribution limit from Step 1 equally between you and your spouse, unless you both agree on a different allocation (such as allocating nothing to one spouse)." The candidate counts forms with f8889.allocation agreed; the project counts them only on forms using the spouse rule (f8889.split). f8889.allocation is asked only within the spouse rule (through f8889.share_raw under f8889.line6_split), so the value differences (classm.f8889.1, classm.f8889.1.deepseek, classm.f5695.2: count 1 against 0) supply an allocation on a non-split form, a record the interview cannot produce, and the 35 candidate-unknown records (stage11.hsa.self_full_year, stage11.hsa.family_55, stage11.hsa.last_month) are interview records where the allocation was rightly not asked. household.hsa_agreed_count is read only by f8889.allocation_bad on a split form, where both counts agree. Triage executable-triage-v1 (triage/person.deepseek.json): 4,445 of 4,647 comparisons agree; 35 candidate-unknown, 167 value.

Ruling: interface gap; i8889 p. 7, Line 6, Step 2: "Divide the refigured contribution limit from Step 1 equally between you and your spouse, unless you both agree on a different allocation (such as allocating nothing to one spouse)." i8889 p. 7, Step 3: "Subtract the part of the contribution limit allocated to your spouse in Step 2 from the amount determined in Step 1." Unknown kind: as in the Claude log, The candidate sums f8889.share, the published field that carries the f8889.allocation_bad refusal; that gate reads household.hsa_share_sum, which sums person.hsa_share, so the candidate's line depends on itself ("cycle at person[spouse].hsa_share", "cycle at household.hsa_share_sum"; classm.f8889.1, classm.f8889.1.deepseek, classm.f5695.2) whenever the gate evaluates its agreed-allocation test. The published interface listed f8889.share_raw and f8889.share by id, form and type only, with no label or dependency, so the candidate could not tell the pre-check share from the checked one; the source reading (each spouse's part under Steps 2 and 3) is the one the project encodes with share_raw. Value kind: representation (classm.asset.1 $356.25 against $0.00, classm.f5695.7, classm.sc.1; non-split forms), because person.hsa_step1 and person.hsa_share feed only household.hsa_step1_sum and household.hsa_share_sum, which are read only in the third disjunct of f8889.allocation_bad (agreed allocation with different Step 1 limits or more than Step 1 allocated). That gate is reached only through f8889.share on a form with f8889.split true; if only one spouse's form is split, household.hsa_split_count is 1 and the gate is already true; if both are split, the project's split filter keeps both forms and the unfiltered sum is the same (one form per person, more than one refused by person.hsa_repeated). So the filtered and unfiltered sums cannot give a different printed amount. Refusal kind: scope; h_hsa_unsupported_any refusals (classm.carloan.1, classm.f8959.1, stage11.refuse.hsa_screen) match the project's f8889.unsupported refusal at f8889.line13 and line16, and allocation_bad refusals (stage13.refuse.hsa_family_one_spouse) are returns the project refuses at f8889.share. kinds_by_return places 2 candidate refusals on returns the full interview completes (not among the recorded witnesses); they follow from the same field choice, the candidate reaching f8889.allocation_bad through f8889.share on a form the project never reads it for, and are covered by the interface-gap ruling. Triage executable-triage-v1 (triage/person.deepseek.json): 3,953 of 4,647 comparisons agree; 116 candidate-refuses, 201 candidate-unknown, 377 value.

Ruling: scope; i8889 p. 7, Line 6, Step 2: "Divide the refigured contribution limit from Step 1 equally between you and your spouse, unless you both agree on a different allocation (such as allocating nothing to one spouse)." Value kind: representation, as in the Claude log; the candidate's unfiltered sum differs only on non-split forms (classm.asset.1 $712.50 against $0.00, classm.f5695.7, classm.sc.1 spouse), and person.hsa_step1 and person.hsa_share feed only household.hsa_step1_sum and household.hsa_share_sum, which are read only in the third disjunct of f8889.allocation_bad (agreed allocation with different Step 1 limits or more than Step 1 allocated). That gate is reached only through f8889.share on a form with f8889.split true; if only one spouse's form is split, household.hsa_split_count is 1 and the gate is already true; if both are split, the project's split filter keeps both forms and the unfiltered sum is the same (one form per person, more than one refused by person.hsa_repeated). So the filtered and unfiltered sums cannot give a different printed amount. Refusal kind: the candidate refuses on person.h_hsa_unsupported_any (f8889.unsupported) where the project's helper is zero (classm.carloan.1, classm.f8959.1, stage11.refuse.hsa_screen, stage16.refuse.f8889.unsupported_part2); the project refuses the same answer at f8889.line13 and f8889.line16 ("Form 8889 Part III, Form 8853, or other HSA situations", cited i8889 Parts II and III), which every return with a Form 8889 evaluates for Schedule 1 line 13. The 2 candidate-unknown records (stage16.hsa.partial.H01/H02) lack dec_coverage. Triage executable-triage-v1 (triage/person.deepseek.json): 4,172 of 4,647 comparisons agree; 86 candidate-refuses, 2 candidate-unknown, 387 value.

Ruling: model error; i4562 p. 5, Line 11: the business income limit is "the total taxable income from any trade or business you actively conducted, computed without regard to any section 179 expense deduction, the deduction for one-half of self-employment taxes under section 164(f), or any net operating loss deduction." The candidate copies person.sc_total (Schedule C line 31 after the section 179 deduction); the project sums sc.line31_pre179. Besides being the wrong amount, it makes the candidate graph circular: sc.line31 reads the section 179 deduction, limited by s179.income, which reads person.income179 ("cycle at person[taxpayer].sc_total" on classm.asset.2, classm.asset.3, classm.f8889.2.deepseek, where the project gives -$146,829.84, $107,211.44, -$27,941.80). The candidate's s179.mfs refusals (classm.f8959.2, stage14.s179.refuse_mfs) are on married-filing-separately returns the project refuses at scope.ready; the project refusals (stage14.ho.refuse_8829, stage14.refuse.statutory, classm.scveh.5) are cited Schedule C screens. Triage executable-triage-v1 (triage/person.deepseek.json): 3,576 of 4,647 comparisons agree; 53 candidate-refuses, 939 candidate-unknown, 79 project-refuses.

Ruling: scope; f8606 (2025) Part I: "Enter the amount from line 3 on line 14. Do not complete the rest of Part I" when there is no distribution. The candidate takes line 3 without a distribution and the f8606.line14 total otherwise, the project the f8606.line14 total (line 3, refused on a distribution); same value. Triage cannot evaluate it: the 4,555 candidate-unknown records are the cycle inherited from person.ira_deduction. The 11 or 12 project refusals are the cited Pub. 590-A refusals (stage16.refuse.ira.both_kinds, stage16.refuse.ira.kbh_short, stage16.refuse.person.ira_over_limit, stage16.refuse.ira.over_comp). The at-risk refusal (stage14.refuse.at_risk; i1040sc p. 15, Line 32, "Be sure to attach Form 6198 to your return") is a cited scope refusal. The candidate declares refusals on person.se_screen and person.rrta for every person; the project asks se_screen only of a person with a Schedule C and refuses railroad compensation only together with a business (person.se_rrta). For a person with no Schedule C the Schedule SE conditions the screen lists that can arise without one (church employee income, clergy income, partnership self-employment income, farm income) are refused by scope.schedule1 and other earned income by scope.other_income, and railroad compensation alone gives no self-employment tax (the project refuses it at person.credit through Schedule 3 line 11 on every return).
